title: Missed dplyr::mapvalues()
description:
I was fiddling around with plydata, and I wanted to map some non-categorial data columns. For plotine, I often have the problem that I have to rename values to get proper labels. With dplyr, there is dplyr::mapvalues(), which is was missing in plydata. My quick hack for that looks like this:

```python
def mapvalues(column, keys=None, values=None, na_action=None, **kwargs):
    translate_dict = None
    if keys is not None:
        assert values is not None and len(keys) == len(values)
        translate_dict = dict(zip(keys, values))
    else:
        assert kwargs is not None
        translate_dict = kwargs
    def mapper(df):
        return df[column].map(translate_dict, na_action=na_action)
    return mapper
```

Usage:
```
>> plydata.data.fishdata >> define(Station_X=mapvalues('Station', ['Release', 'MAW'], ['Foobar', "Barfoo"]))
    TagID  Station  value Station_X
0    4842  Release      1    Foobar
1    4843  Release      1    Foobar
2    4844  Release      1    Foobar
3    4845  Release      1    Foobar
4    4847  Release      1    Foobar
..    ...      ...    ...       ...
204  4861      MAW      1    Barfoo
205  4862      MAW      0    Barfoo
206  4863      MAW      0    Barfoo
207  4864      MAW      0    Barfoo
208  4865      MAW      0    Barfoo

[209 rows x 4 columns]
```

If there is a better way or a package that already provides this, just let me know. Otherwise, I think it would be a good addition to plydata.

title: separate gives unintended output when index is not standard range
description:
version 0.4.3

This works as intended
```
separate(pd.DataFrame({'a':[1,2,3], 'name':['a_b_c', 'd_e_f', 'g_h_i']}),
         'name', into=['x','y','z'])
```

This mangles the output, even column a is affected.

title: Need to include 'IPython.sphinxext.ipython_console_highlighting' in doc/conf.py extensions list
description:
Hi, I've been trying to build the documentation and I'm getting lots of warnings "doc/tutorials/dealing-with-nan-values.ipynb:: WARNING: Pygments lexer name 'ipython3' is not known".  I found a solution at https://github.com/spatialaudio/nbsphinx/issues/24 - one just needs to add `'IPython.sphinxext.ipython_console_highlighting'` to the list of extensions in `doc/conf.py`.  The same goes for `plotnine`.

Best wishes, Julian

title: Referring to data outside of the data frame?
description:
In R, I can do this:
```
library(dplyr)
df = data.frame(x=c("a", "a", "b", "b", "c"), y=c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5))

letters_of_interest = c("a", "c")
df %>% filter(x %in% letters_of_interest)
  x y
1 a 1
2 a 2
3 c 5
```

In plydata, I thought this would work:
```
import pandas as pd
from plydata import query
df = pd.DataFrame({'x': ['a', 'a', 'b', 'b', 'c'], 'y': [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]})
letters_of_interest = ['a', 'c']
df >> query('x.isin(letters_of_interest)')
# ...
KeyError: 'letters_of_interest'
pandas.core.computation.ops.UndefinedVariableError: name 'letters_of_interest' is not defined
```

Perhaps it's obvious, but on a whim I tried this, which does work:
```
 df >> query(f'x.isin({letters_of_interest})')
   x  y
0  a  1
1  a  2
4  c  5
```

Is there somewhere that what is quoted vs. what is not is systematized? Maybe I just haven't wrapped my head around it, but I find it hard to remember what needs quotes (e.g. `query('col_name == "foo"')`) vs. what is not (e.g. `summarize(new_col_name = 'np.mean(col_name')`). Is there a good way to identify that plydata needs quotes around and/or is the above obvious from the documentation somewhere (perhaps "pulling in variables from the dataframe are accessible, but external variables need to be string formatted")?

Thanks.

description:

This had me quite confused:
```

2

3
```

title: groupby and summarize is extremly slow for large number of groups
description:
Why is groupby + summarize so slow compared to simple pandas. Please find the reproducible example.

```
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from plydata import *

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": np.random.choice(100000, 1000000, replace = True)
                   , "b": np.random.normal(10, 2, 1000000)}
                 )
df

%%time
# with plydata
res = (df >>
  group_by("a") >>
  summarise(c = "mean(b)" , d = "std(b)")
  )
res # took around ~ 7 mins

%%time
# plain pandas
df.groupby("a").agg(c = ("b", np.mean), d = ("b", np.std)).reset_index() # took 122 ms
```

title: add spread() and gather() functions?
description:
Just started playing with this package today and it looks really great. I was wondering if it would be possible to implement some functions for `spread()` and `gather()`. I took a quick shot at it and put together some functions that can be used with `call()` (borrowing some code from [this blog post](http://connor-johnson.com/2014/08/28/tidyr-and-pandas-gather-and-melt/)):

```python
def gather( df, key, value, cols ):
    id_vars = [ col for col in df.columns if col not in cols ]
    id_values = cols
    var_name = key
    value_name = value
    return pd.melt( df, id_vars, id_values, var_name, value_name )

def spread( df, index, columns, values ):
    return df.pivot(index, columns, values).reset_index(level=index).rename_axis(None,axis=1)

# minimal example
names = [ 'Wilbur', 'Petunia', 'Gregory' ]
a = [ 67, 80, 64 ]
b = [ 56, 90, 50 ]
df = pd.DataFrame({'names':names,'a':a,'b':b})

df_long = (df 
  >> call(gather, "drug", "heartrate", ["a","b"])
)

df_wide = (df_long
  >> call(spread, "names", "drug", "heartrate")
)
```

These work ok, but it would be even nicer to have these functions built-in and perhaps being able to be used directly, e.g.:

```df >> gather("drug", "heartrate",["a","b"])```


title: define throws error when accessing column named 'n'
description:
```python
from plydata import (define, rename, query)
df = pd.DataFrame({'n': [1,2,3]})
df >> define(y = 'n+1')
```
throws TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'function' and 'int'
query function has no issues with it though.
```python
from plydata import (define, rename, query)
df = pd.DataFrame({'n': [1,2,3]})
df >> query('n>1')
```

title: query function is not able to access variables. (UndefinedVariableError: name 'y' is not defined)
description:
Hi !

Not sure if this is a technical limitation, but query function is not able to access the values of variables. define function does not have this problem.

This works.
```python
df = pd.DataFrame({'x': [1,2,3]})
df >> query('x > 2')
```
This doesn't.
```python
y = 2
df = pd.DataFrame({'x': [1,2,3]})
df >> query('x > y')
```
For now, I'm doing this instead -
```python
df >> query('x > {}'.format(y))
```

In the case of define, it works as expected.
```python
y = 2
df = pd.DataFrame({'x': [1,2,3]})
df >> define(sum = 'x + y')
```
